edges.description: The severe neonatal ZSD presentation includes hypotonia as an early neuromuscular manifestation of peroxisome biogenesis failure.
Severe neonatal ZSD often causes poor feeding, linking the multisystem neonatal phenotype to nutritional compromise.
Congenital neuronal migration defects in severe ZSD produce neonatal-onset seizures.
Severe ZSD includes distinctive craniofacial dysmorphism as part of the congenital malformation spectrum.
Peroxisomal bile-acid and lipid metabolism failure manifests clinically as liver involvement, including hepatomegaly, in severe and milder ZSD.
Severe ZSD includes renal cysts among the congenital malformations associated with peroxisome biogenesis failure.
Severe ZSD includes bony stippling of the patellae and long bones, captured clinically as chondrodysplasia punctata.
Progressive peroxisome dysfunction causes sensory loss that includes sensorineural hearing impairment.
Progressive peroxisome dysfunction causes retinal dystrophy, represented in the pathograph as retinal degeneration/retinitis pigmentosa.
Progressive peroxisome dysfunction causes neurologic involvement that includes leukodystrophy.
Progressive neurologic involvement in intermediate/milder ZSD includes ataxia.
Progressive neurologic involvement in intermediate/milder ZSD includes polyneuropathy.
The neurologic impact of ZSD commonly includes developmental delay, although intellect can be normal at the mildest end.
Progressive peroxisome dysfunction includes adrenal insufficiency, particularly in milder ZSD presentations.
Progressive peroxisome dysfunction can include renal oxalate stones.
Some individuals with ZSD have reduced bone mineral density.
Dental enamel involvement in secondary teeth is a common ZSD manifestation.
Failure to recognise matrix cargo in the cytosol leaves the peroxisome an empty membrane compartment, the import-competence failure this node feeds.
Loss of receptor docking blocks translocation of matrix enzymes across the peroxisomal membrane, the import-competence failure this node feeds.
Failure to ubiquitinate and retrotranslocate the import receptor depletes the recyclable receptor pool, the import-competence failure this node feeds.
Failure to export the import receptor back to the cytosol stalls the import cycle after a single round, the import-competence failure this node feeds.
Absence of a peroxisomal membrane compartment is the most complete form of peroxisome biogenesis failure, since neither membrane nor matrix proteins reach an organelle.
Reduced peroxisome division lowers the peroxisomal complement of the cell, a milder and mechanistically distinct route into the same organelle-level insufficiency.

nodes.description: PEX3, PEX16 and PEX19 are the three mammalian peroxins dedicated to inserting peroxisomal membrane proteins into the peroxisomal membrane, by a PEX19- and PEX3-dependent class I route and a PEX19- and PEX16-dependent class II route. Their loss is categorically different from a matrix import defect: in the absence of any of the three no peroxisomal structures can be identified at all, and peroxisomal membrane proteins are mistargeted or degraded, so there is no membrane compartment left for the import machinery to act on.

nodes.description: PEX2, PEX10 and PEX12 are the three RING finger peroxins of a membrane-embedded ubiquitin ligase complex. The complex monoubiquitinates the import receptor after cargo release and forms the channel through which the receptor is retrotranslocated back to the cytosol; when recycling is compromised the receptor is instead polyubiquitinated and degraded. Biallelic loss of any of the three therefore exhausts the receptor pool and stops further import.

nodes.description: The receptor export module resets the import machinery. PEX1 and PEX6 are its two AAA+ ATPases and PEX26 the membrane protein that anchors them to the organelle. Unlike most translocases, peroxisomal matrix import does not use ATP hydrolysis to move cargo; it uses it only to extract the receptor afterwards, which is why losing this module stalls the cycle rather than the individual translocation event. PEX1 variants are among the most prevalent reported in this spectrum.
